items.stem: An agent reports 'task complete'. What confirms the task actually succeeded?

options.text: Verifying the claimed result and actions against an independent source of truth
options.rationale: Correct: independent verification confirms real outcomes, not just the agent's claim.

options.text: The agent repeating that it is confident
options.rationale: Self-reported confidence is not evidence of success.

options.text: A longer final message from the agent
options.rationale: Message length does not verify an outcome.

options.text: The agent using the newest model
options.rationale: Model version does not confirm a result.

items.explanation: Correct: independent verification confirms real outcomes, not just the agent's claim.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Why define checkpoints with success criteria before launching an agent?

options.text: So each step can be judged and the run corrected early
options.rationale: Correct: checkpoints give objective points to supervise and intervene.
Checkpoints are about control, not speed.

options.text: So no human is ever needed
options.rationale: Checkpoints support human supervision rather than removing it.

options.text: To reduce the token price per call
options.rationale: Checkpoints do not change per-call pricing.

items.explanation: Correct: checkpoints give objective points to supervise and intervene.

items.stem: Which TWO guardrails limit the damage an agent can do if it goes off-track? (Select TWO)

options.text: A scoped permission boundary the agent cannot cross
options.rationale: Correct: limiting scope caps what the agent is able to affect.

options.text: A stop condition that escalates to a human
options.rationale: Correct: a stop/escalation condition halts runaway behaviour.
Removing logging hides what the agent did and worsens control.

options.text: Granting the agent broad write access
options.rationale: Broad write access increases potential damage.

items.explanation: Correct: limiting scope caps what the agent is able to affect.
